newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle sales thin at $68 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle sales thin at $68 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold in thin trade at $68.00 per cwt, unchanged from top prices paid in active trade earlier this week, feedlot sources said.
About 1,500 head of slaughter steers and heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, sources there said.
The sales followed a weekly movement of 104,500 head, USDA satistics showed.
An estimated 500 head sold in Kansas, also steers and heifers that will likely grade select and choice. Weekly movement there was pegged at 105,200 head by USDA.
Prices this week were underpinned by firm beef demand and tight packer inventories, with many cattle sold this week picked up within a day or two of purchase, sources said.
Several cattle feeders said their lots wer very current after some pulled cattle ahead to meet this week's strong packer demand.
Showlists next week were expected to be unchanged to smaller than this week's, sporting a larger percentage of 'green' or unfinished cattle, some cattle feeders said.
Fed cattle early next week were expected to be priced from $69.00 to $70.00, they said.
